  - paragraph: Square 16-QAM carries four bits per symbol and has unit average symbol energy with this scaling. Amplitude compression and phase errors both distort its decision regions.
  - heading "APSK satellite constellations" [level=2]
  - paragraph: sₖ = rℓ exp(jθₖ); Es = Σℓ Nℓrℓ²/M
  - paragraph: 16-APSK uses 4+12 points on two rings; 32-APSK uses 4+12+16 on three. Ring ratios and phase offsets depend on the design. The simulator uses illustrative ratios 1:2.53:4.30, not a full DVB-S2 implementation.
  - heading "FSK and GMSK" [level=2]
  - paragraph: x[n] = exp(jφ[n]); φ[n] = φ[n−1] + 2πf[n]/Fs
  - paragraph: Frequency-shift keying encodes information in frequency. The BFSK default is continuous phase with h=0.5; deviation and continuity are configurable. GMSK always uses h=0.5 and Gaussian-filters the NRZ frequency pulse at configurable BT (default 0.3) before phase integration; both have a constant clean envelope. They have no fixed discrete I/Q constellation.
  - heading "SNR and AWGN" [level=2]
  - paragraph: SNRdB = 10 log₁₀(Ps/Pn); σ²I = σ²Q = Pn/2
  - paragraph: Complex AWGN splits noise power equally between I and Q. Es/N₀, Eb/N₀, and sample SNR are different quantities; conversion depends on bits per symbol and samples per symbol.
  - heading "RRC pulse shaping" [level=2]
  - paragraph: B ≈ (1+α)Rs; 0 < α ≤ 1
  - paragraph: Root-raised-cosine transmit and receive filters combine to a raised-cosine response. Finite filter span and timing error can still introduce intersymbol interference. FSK/GMSK use their own frequency pulse shaping.
  - heading "Satellite Doppler and carrier offset" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Δf = −(vr/c)fc; x′[n] = x[n] exp(j2πΔf n/Fs)
  - paragraph: Range rate shifts carrier frequency during a LEO pass. A fixed receiver oscillator error adds CFO. Studio applies a constant offset over a short capture; the orbital explorer below shows an approximate time-varying pass.
  - heading "Phase noise and Rician fading" [level=2]
  - paragraph: h = √(K/(K+1)) + (a+jb)/√(2(K+1))
  - paragraph: K is a linear line-of-sight to scattered-power ratio. K=0 gives Rayleigh fading when enabled. The simulator supports independent scatter per configurable sample block and either independent phase jitter or a Wiener phase walk. It does not model a Doppler-correlated scattering process.
  - heading "Saleh TWTA amplifier" [level=2]
  - paragraph: A(r) = αa r/(1+βa r²); Φ(r) = αφ r²/(1+βφ r²)
  - paragraph: Traveling-wave tube saturation changes amplitude and phase. The simulator applies both AM/AM and AM/PM distortion before fading and AWGN. More amplitude levels can increase sensitivity to nonlinear distortion.
  - heading "CNN automatic modulation classification" [level=2]
  - paragraph: p = softmax(Wz+b); H(p) = −Σk pk log₂(pk)
  - paragraph: The supplied CNN reads 128×2 I/Q windows after the saved scalar z-score transform. Three convolution blocks, batch normalization, pooling, and dense layers estimate BPSK, QPSK, and 16-QAM probabilities. Entropy is ambiguity within those three classes, not a calibrated unknown-signal detector.

  - heading "Complex I/Q signals" [level=2]
  - paragraph: x[n] = I[n] + jQ[n]; |x| = √(I² + Q²); φ = atan2(Q, I)
  - paragraph: Two orthogonal components preserve amplitude and phase at baseband. Sample rate determines the physical frequency axis. Sample amplitudes are relative unless the receiver is calibrated.
  - heading "Digital modulation" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Rb = Rs log₂(M)
  - paragraph: Symbols select waveforms from an alphabet of size M. Bit rate depends on symbol rate and modulation order before coding overhead; spectral efficiency also depends on pulse shaping.
  - heading "BPSK" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "sₖ = exp(jπk), k ∈ {0, 1}"
  - paragraph: Two antipodal phases encode one bit per symbol. Ideal coherent AWGN BER is Q(√(2Eb/N₀)). Accurate carrier recovery is required.
  - heading "QPSK and M-PSK" [level=2]
  - paragraph: sₖ = exp(j(2πk/M + θ₀))
  - paragraph: QPSK has four phases and two bits per symbol; 8-PSK carries three. Higher order PSK narrows angular decision margins. Gray coding reduces bit errors between adjacent symbols.
  - heading "Quadrature amplitude modulation" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "16-QAM: I,Q ∈ {−3,−1,1,3}/√10"
  - paragraph: Square 16-QAM carries four bits per symbol and has unit average symbol energy with this scaling. Amplitude compression and phase errors both distort its decision regions.
  - heading "APSK satellite constellations" [level=2]
  - paragraph: sₖ = rℓ exp(jθₖ); Es = Σℓ Nℓrℓ²/M
  - paragraph: 16-APSK uses 4+12 points on two rings; 32-APSK uses 4+12+16 on three. Ring ratios and phase offsets depend on the design. The simulator uses illustrative ratios 1:2.53:4.30, not a full DVB-S2 implementation.
  - heading "FSK and GMSK" [level=2]
  - paragraph: x[n] = exp(jφ[n]); φ[n] = φ[n−1] + 2πf[n]/Fs
  - paragraph: Frequency-shift keying encodes information in frequency. The BFSK default is continuous phase with h=0.5; deviation and continuity are configurable. GMSK always uses h=0.5 and Gaussian-filters the NRZ frequency pulse at configurable BT (default 0.3) before phase integration; both have a constant clean envelope. They have no fixed discrete I/Q constellation.
  - heading "SNR and AWGN" [level=2]
  - paragraph: SNRdB = 10 log₁₀(Ps/Pn); σ²I = σ²Q = Pn/2
  - paragraph: Complex AWGN splits noise power equally between I and Q. Es/N₀, Eb/N₀, and sample SNR are different quantities; conversion depends on bits per symbol and samples per symbol.
  - heading "RRC pulse shaping" [level=2]
  - paragraph: B ≈ (1+α)Rs; 0 < α ≤ 1
  - paragraph: Root-raised-cosine transmit and receive filters combine to a raised-cosine response. Finite filter span and timing error can still introduce intersymbol interference. FSK/GMSK use their own frequency pulse shaping.
  - heading "Satellite Doppler and carrier offset" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Δf = −(vr/c)fc; x′[n] = x[n] exp(j2πΔf n/Fs)
  - paragraph: Range rate shifts carrier frequency during a LEO pass. A fixed receiver oscillator error adds CFO. Studio applies a constant offset over a short capture; the orbital explorer below shows an approximate time-varying pass.
  - heading "Phase noise and Rician fading" [level=2]
  - paragraph: h = √(K/(K+1)) + (a+jb)/√(2(K+1))
  - paragraph: K is a linear line-of-sight to scattered-power ratio. K=0 gives Rayleigh fading when enabled. The simulator supports independent scatter per configurable sample block and either independent phase jitter or a Wiener phase walk. It does not model a Doppler-correlated scattering process.
  - heading "Saleh TWTA amplifier" [level=2]
  - paragraph: A(r) = αa r/(1+βa r²); Φ(r) = αφ r²/(1+βφ r²)
  - paragraph: Traveling-wave tube saturation changes amplitude and phase. The simulator applies both AM/AM and AM/PM distortion before fading and AWGN. More amplitude levels can increase sensitivity to nonlinear distortion.
  - heading "CNN automatic modulation classification" [level=2]
  - paragraph: p = softmax(Wz+b); H(p) = −Σk pk log₂(pk)
  - paragraph: The supplied CNN reads 128×2 I/Q windows after the saved scalar z-score transform. Three convolution blocks, batch normalization, pooling, and dense layers estimate BPSK, QPSK, and 16-QAM probabilities. Entropy is ambiguity within those three classes, not a calibrated unknown-signal detector.
